chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام about the sick person: should tawaf of the Ka'bah be performed on his behalf? He said: No; rather, he should be taken around it.

key_terms.الْمَرِيضِ: the sick person under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.بِالْكَعْبَةِ: around the Ka'bah, the sacred sanctuary
key_terms.بِهِ: with him, meaning the sick person is to be carried or taken
key_terms.عَنْهُ: on his behalf, in substitution for him
key_terms.لَا: a negation indicating the ruling's prohibition here
key_terms.يُطَافُ: tawaf is performed; going around the Ka'bah ritually

ai.seo_question: Can tawaf be performed on behalf of a sick person, or must the sick person be taken around the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding tawaf for a sick person. It states that tawaf is not to be performed merely on his behalf; rather, if possible, the sick person himself is to be carried or taken around the Ka'bah.
